newsitem.title: INDIA: India train crash toll rises to 13.
newsitem.headline: India train crash toll rises to 13.

text.p: The driver of a train that ploughed into another near New Delhi has died, raising the death toll in the disaster to 13, doctors and police said on Tuesday.
"The driver of the Karnataka Express died today," said an official at the railway police station in Faridabad, on the outskirts of the Indian capital.
Railway officials said Monday's disaster was caused by human error when the speeding Karnataka Express overshot a stop signal on a loop line and rammed into the slower-moving Himsagar Express.
Railway officials said rail services had largely resumed on Tuesday through Faridabad, an important junction.
A similar accident occurred in Faridabad in May when a passenger train overshot a stop signal and crashed into a freight train. No casualties were reported in that accident.
Latest government figures show 594 people died in 398 railway accidents in 1995/96 (April-March), compared with 305 deaths in 501 accidents the previous year.

India's railways cover a vast network spread over 62,915 km (39,321 miles) and in 1995/96 carried 123 million passengers on long-distance journeys. Trains are the cheapest mode of transport across the huge country.
In August 1995, at least 350 people were killed in India's worst train accident.
